claims.text: OC 186A extends UPI Tap & Pay via NFC from QR-based transactions to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals, allowing users to make contactless payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on the terminal.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
Payee PSPs are required to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) at all PoS terminals under their acquiring network.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals shall be accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Remitter Banks must validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
Members and UPI Application Providers shall consult with Users to provide an option to set their own transaction limits within a ceiling of ₹5000.
A per-transaction limit of ₹5000 is capped, up to which no additional factor of authentication is required.
Explicit User consent must be obtained for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with Users having the ability to opt out at any time.
Device lock must be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
UPI Application Providers shall present UPI Tap & Pay through a dedicated call-to-action as a standalone feature, not embedded within other services or menu categories.

claims.text: The available OC 185 series documents do not establish a 25 lakh limit for UPI tax payments; they specify a per transaction limit of Rs 5 lakh.
Under circular NPCI/UPI/2024-25/OC-185A, the per transaction value limit for entities under categories aligned to tax payments is enhanced to Rs 5 lakh.
Under circular NPCI/UPI/2025-26/OC-185B, the per transaction limits for entities under categories aligned to Tax Payments are increased to Rs 5 lakh.
The enhanced limit of Rs 5 lakh applies only to 'Verified Merchants' in the applicable category.
For Government e-Market Place (EMD Payments) under MCC 9311, the enhanced per transaction limit is Rs 5 lakh with a cumulative 24-hour limit of Rs 10 lakh.
Acquiring entities must ensure that classification within MCC-9311 strictly adheres to tax payments only for the enhanced limit to apply.
